title: Floor-level holdout leak — the ESTIMAND closed for the 2 kanto pairs
campaign: reasoning-surface follow-up (round 6). NAMING COLLISION, stated rather than renamed: logs/phase_r6_llm_channel_audit.json already occupies the phase_r6_ prefix for the unrelated LLM-channel audit cited by generic_reasoning.py's header. This receipt keeps the briefed filename; the two are distinct artifacts and neither supersedes the other.

adjudication.verdict: WRONG_ARM — the brief prescribed a floor-side guard that cannot exist; landed as arm (1) estimand-side quarantine instead.
adjudication.brief_as_written: Close that leak at the hydrate floor: drop floor surfaces whose constituent edges include a holdout edge.
adjudication.why_that_arm_matches_nothing: generic_expand renders ONE TRIPLE PER LINE and has no composition surface ('every line is one verified triple; no invention, no LLM', generic_expand.py:10-12). Each floor surface's single edge IS a train edge, so a guard keyed on 'constituent edges include a holdout edge' has an empty match set by construction. The leak is at the CLASS-PAIR level: a TRAIN triple and a HOLDOUT triple share an endpoint class pair under a different predicate or in the reverse direction.
adjudication.why_the_mirror_arm_is_refused: Dropping the floor LINES that state the pair un-teaches 4 real train triples to protect 2 probes. That inverts the estimand — the probe exists to measure the training, not the reverse.

binding_prior_art.quote: I widened the holdout-bridge scan to include adjacent pairs... an adjacent pair IS one of the walk's own TRAIN triples, and the deterministic floor renders those verbatim anyway, so refusing to render the walk cannot change whether the corpus states that holdout class pair. Both pairs it fired on were already stated by the floor (2 and 3 lines). Cost: 1,542 walks and 4 of 521 train triples. Delta on its own instrument: zero.
binding_prior_art.defended_by: scripts/pipeline/test_generic_reasoning.py::test_holdout_stated_as_the_walks_own_adjacent_edge_is_NOT_dropped_and_why — asserts PRESENT behaviour, so re-adding the reverted arm fails the suite. Left untouched; the module still prints ALL 58 REASONING-SURFACE TESTS PASS.
binding_prior_art.the_item_this_receipt_closes: That commit named the upstream leak: 'the hydrate floor renders 475 of 521 train triples and thereby states 2 of the 72 holdout class pairs outright. No walk-level guard can fix that.'

adjudication.arm_2_split_cut_prevention: REJECTED and its red_green line struck. No split may be re-cut in this item, so a cutting change moves no instrument here — the exact false-landing shape of the round-4 revert. Secondary: class-pair closure at cut time unions every entity pair carrying >= 2 relations into one group, and larger groups trip the existing zero-a-predicate-train-side guard more often, making well-connected pairs systematically less likely to be held out — a measured bias traded for an unmeasured one. Tertiary: `opposes` is absent from split._INVERSE_PAIRS and adding it would fix only pair 1 while redefining a version label with 99 written manifests, against split.py's own law that a new split is a new version file, never a rewrite. DETECTION kept; CUTTING dropped.
